articles.dek: Community-dynamics metrics (Hallett et al., MEE 2016), promoted on Jared's 2026-11-13 approval of rank clocks. Stage 2–3 on the real panels has not been run.
articles.verdict: promoted (scout evidence; Stage 2–3 not yet run)

articles.title: Scout: weight-free dominance ranking shows which stress-test trade-offs payouts actually follow
articles.dek: Partial-order ranking with exact rank probabilities from network science and environmental chemistry (Schoch, Social Networks 2018; netrankr 2.0.0), run on public stress-test results for Q3: 13 severely adverse exercises 2013–2025, 360 firm-years. Where one firm is worse on all three indicators it paid out less in 71.5% of 2,203 pairs (null 50%, p = 0.0002). 55% of pairs are trade-offs; there, payouts follow pre-tax income (0.639) and run against the loan-loss rate (0.409), which an equal-weight composite averages to 0.552. In 2021–25 pairs where the SCB disagrees with the path, payouts follow the path in 78.9%. Walk-forward miss: 0.36 vs OLS 0.46, ARDL 0.67, SARIMAX 0.65. netrankr vignette reproduced. Scout status: recommend; not started.

articles.title: Scout: comparative-biology signal tests show noise hides half the program hierarchy's growth signal
articles.dek: Blomberg's K, Pagel's λ and local indicators of phylogenetic association (Keck et al., Ecology and Evolution 2016; phylosignal 1.3.1), run on the SYNTHETIC mock ZBB datasets for Q2 with the label hierarchy as the tree. λ of per-program growth is 0.52 vs 1.22 noise-free (Corning-like) and 0.78 vs 1.12 (MS-like); a scrubbed-text tree carries less (0.35, 0.57). A relatives' mean beats a per-program OLS trend by 7.2% and 14.3% RMSE, about as well as ARDL(1). LIPA misses on mismatch (AUC 0.59, 0.53 vs OLS 0.74, 0.65) and drift. Brownian checks reproduced. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: climate-science information flow finds spread moves feed fails uncertainty, but its built-in test is just Granger
articles.dek: Liang–Kleeman information flow from climate dynamics (Liang, Entropy 2021; LK_Info_flow 3.1.2.1), run on public repo aggregates for Q1: 399 weeks 2018–2025 of fails, DVP and tri-party volumes, the DVP − tri-party spread, leveraged-fund positioning and VIX. Spread moves precede fails and raise their uncertainty (τ +1.7%, bootstrap p = 0.033) and damp DVP volume (τ −3.6%, p = 0.013); none survive Holm. Positioning → fails is Granger-significant (p = 0.012) with no flow (τ −0.10%). The package's test equals the lag-1 Granger t and rejects true-zero links 14–20% of the time on these series. Monthly Form PF: no flow. Walk-forward miss (−2.4% RMSE, DM p = 0.57). Liang (2021) network reproduced within 0.4 pp. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: necessity ceilings show the stressed capital trough gates payouts; the SCB almost never binds
articles.dek: Necessary Condition Analysis from organization science (Dul, ORM 2016; Dul, van der Laan & Kuik, ORM 2020; NCA 5.1.0), run on public stress-test results for Q3: 13 severely adverse exercises 2013–2025, 360 firm-years. The stressed minimum CET1 ratio caps payout/RWA beyond what its correlation produces (d 0.245 vs 95th pct 0.211 under a Gaussian-copula null, p = 0.012; within-year p = 0.0002), also for dividends and buybacks. The drawdown passes the standard NCA test but its ceiling is correlation-made (p = 0.48). The trough binds for 69% of firm-years, the SCB for 1.5%. The default NCA test calls correlated-only data necessary 56–74% of the time at ρ 0.3. Misses: total payout fragile to the top-2% trim; envelope looser than a 95% quantile line. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: a genomics short-series miner says which budget shapes are real, where k-means just returns clusters
articles.dek: STEM from genomics (Ernst, Nau & Bar-Joseph, Bioinformatics 2005; Ernst & Bar-Joseph, BMC Bioinformatics 2006; stem.jar 1.3.15), run on the SYNTHETIC mock ZBB datasets for Q2. 7 and 5 of 50 fixed shapes are over-represented on the Corning-like and MS-like mocks; with years shuffled, 1 and 0, while k-means still returns 10 and 5 clusters. Using the budget as a same-year replicate (exploratory) lifts the share of programs on their noise-free shape from 0.31 to 0.47 and 0.75 to 0.82. K-means at the same k matches or beats it on 5 of 7 planted groups, and its text-vs-numbers flag loses to an OLS slope. Paper simulation reproduced in 20 of 20 seeds; NumPy port identical to the jar. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: a river-chemistry loop index finds repo spreads peak after settlement fails, mostly at quarter-ends
articles.dek: The Lloyd et al. (HESS 2016) hysteresis index and Vaughan et al. (WRR 2017) flushing index from catchment hydrology, run on public weekly repo and settlement-fails aggregates for Q1. In 13 fails storms (2019–2026), the DVP minus tri-party spread lags fails (mean HI −0.17, 6 of 13 storms clearly anticlockwise, none clockwise; circular-shift p = 0.042, Holm 0.126). With quarter-end weeks masked (post hoc) it falls to −0.08 (p = 0.35). DVP volume and leveraged-fund positioning show no loop, and a limb term adds nothing to an ARDL walk-forward (RMSE +0.5%). Lloyd Fig. 1 reproduced exactly. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: climate-impact event coincidence finds financing fails spike a week after leveraged-fund unwinds
articles.dek: Event coincidence analysis from climate-impact science (Donges et al., EPJ ST 2016; CoinCalc 2.0), run on public weekly repo, settlement-fails and CFTC positioning aggregates for Q1. 26% of financing-fails spike weeks come exactly one week after a big leveraged-fund unwind (vs about 10% by chance, circular-shift p = 0.008); builds show nothing and the reverse direction is not significant. The package's Poisson test has a 9.2–9.4% false-positive rate at nominal 5% on these clustered series. Paper examples reproduced exactly. Scout status: recommend for promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Scout: STATIS finds the stress-test and payout pattern split into pre- and post-2020 eras
articles.dek: STATIS from sensory science and ecology (Lavit et al., CSDA 1994; Abdi et al., WIREs 2012; ade4 1.7.24), run on 13 public stress-test exercises (7 variables) for Q3. The joint pattern splits into 2013–19 and 2020–25 eras (exact p = 0.023; modified RV 0.016), with the best cut at 2021 (exploratory); no single pair is familywise significant (max-T p = 0.11), and the year-departure bootstrap was invalid. NumPy core at 3e-13 parity with ade4. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: Taylor’s power law says the mock program books are not as diversified as CV-based measures claim
articles.dek: Mean-variance portfolio effects from fisheries ecology (Anderson, Cooper & Dulvy, Methods in Ecology and Evolution 2013; ecofolio 0.1.0), run on the SYNTHETIC mock ZBB datasets for Q2.3/Q2.4. Program volatility scales with size at Taylor z = 1.67 / 1.77, not 2, so the average-CV portfolio effect (3.36 / 3.25) and the diversification ratio (3.14 / 3.10) overstate stability against the mean-variance effect (0.99 / 1.15). Part of the apparent diversification is noise. It loses to plain correlation as a hidden-group screen. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: probabilistic index models show the stress-test pre-tax path, not the drawdown, orders bank payouts
articles.dek: Probabilistic index models from biostatistics (Thas et al., JRSS-B 2012; pim 2.0.4), run within test years on public Fed stress-test results and FR Y-9C payouts for Q3. A bank with a one-IQR better severely adverse pre-tax path has the higher payout/RWA 68% of the time (Holm p = 0.02); drawdown adds nothing beyond it; the Adverse–SA gap adds nothing. Before 2020 the stress ranking shows up in dividends (Holm p = 0.02); after 2020, weakly, in buybacks. OLS on payout/NI loses 43% of its slope after trimming 2% of ratios; PIM moves under 2%. The scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared’s pick.

articles.title: Scout: convergent cross mapping finds fails and leveraged-fund positioning in the repo spread’s dynamics, not in each other
articles.dek: Convergent cross mapping from fisheries ecology (Sugihara et al., Science 2012; Ye et al., Scientific Reports 2015; pyEDM 2.5.7), run on public CFTC TFF, NY Fed fails and OFR repo aggregates for Q1.5. Weekly fails cross-map the DVP–tri-party spread (ρ = 0.33) and so do leveraged-fund Treasury-futures position changes (ρ = 0.25): shift-null p = 0.005, Holm 0.05 (the 200-surrogate floor), stable across halves. Positioning and fails don’t cross-map either way, though linear Granger rejects both ways. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: archaeological seriation dates the repo market’s venue and tenor mix, and Form PF borrowing growth sets its pace
articles.dek: Correspondence-analysis seriation, Porčić’s significance test, Bellanger–Husi event dates and EPPM battleship plots from archaeology (kairos 2.3.0, tabula 3.3.2), run on public OFR repo and SEC Form PF aggregates for Q1.4. The 9-segment mix orders 101 months almost exactly by date (Spearman −0.96, p < 0.001). A walk-forward mix clock errs by 1.06 years vs 1.92 naive. Form PF total borrowing growth leads the clock’s speed by 3–6 months (r = 0.56, Holm p = 0.009). The scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared’s pick.

articles.title: Scout: cross-recurrence shows when Treasury fails and repo spreads move together, and when they stop
articles.dek: Cross-recurrence quantification analysis (Coco & Dale, Frontiers in Psychology 2014; The R Journal 2021), run on public Form PF, OFR repo and NY Fed fails aggregates for Q1. The run was interrupted on 11-14 and completed on 11-15. Weekly financing fails and the DVP–tri-party spread are anti-recurrent in the same week (p = 0.011), from late 2018 to mid-2025, and not in the late-2025 fails spike. Form PF prime-broker borrowings show no familywise lead or lag. The first pass's windowed null was shift-invariant; that is fixed. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: isotonic distributional regression says the stress path, not the buffer, describes payouts
articles.dek: Isotonic distributional regression (Henzi, Ziegel & Gneiting, JRSS-B 2021; CRAN isodistrreg with a Rust core), run on public Fed stress-test results and FR Y-9C payouts for Q3. The run was interrupted on 11-14 and completed on 11-15. Projected pre-tax income gives 15% CRPS skill over climatology for next payout ranks (p = 0.003). The SCB alone gives none (−1.9%), with 38% of firm-years at the floor. IDR beats OLS on raw payouts, but loses with a 2-D partial order. The scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Scout: ebnm tells which of a thousand noisy budget moves are real
articles.dek: Empirical Bayes normal means (Willwerscheid, Carbonetto & Stephens, Journal of Statistical Software 2025), run on SYNTHETIC mock ZBB budgets for Q2. These are not real budgets. Pooling cuts each program's 2025-level error by 21–26%. lfsr < 0.05 calls 91 real year-on-year moves on the Corning mock, all with the right sign, where BH calls 14. It does not help on text vs numbers. The scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Scout: DenseLines draws a thousand short budget lines as one density, once made gap-safe
articles.dek: Density line charts (Moritz & Fisher, arXiv 2018), run on SYNTHETIC mock ZBB budgets for Q2. The NumPy port matches the authors' Rust reference pixel for pixel (max rel. diff 2.1e-7) but is 10–120× slower. The reference renders start/stop portfolios as all-NaN. A residual brush plus a text keyword finds 94% of a hidden AI-demand group, but the brush is bandwidth-fragile. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scheduled scout (catch-up): ecotraj finds a directional residual walk in trading-asset shares
articles.dek: Ecological trajectory analysis (De Cáceres et al., Ecological Monographs 2019), run on a PROXY Y-9C dealer panel. Residual (non-market) clr increments on 14-dealer trading assets are directional (dir 0.595, sign-flip p = 0.008). On equity revenue the GS→JPM swap sits in residual net, but the path is not directional (sign-flip p = 0.664). Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Scheduled scout (catch-up): lphom cannot identify a quarterly share-flow matrix from this single panel
articles.dek: Linear-programming voter-transfer matrices (Pavía & Romero, Sociological Methods & Research 2024). On consecutive quarters of the PROXY equity-revenue panel the matrix is not identified (median bound width 0.88); a planted 1% GS→JPM flow is not recovered. The method needs Form ADV filers as voting units. Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Ad hoc scout: codyn rank clocks and a variance ratio from ecology, aimed at Q1
articles.dek: Community-dynamics metrics (Hallett et al., Methods in Ecology and Evolution 2016), run on a PROXY Y-9C dealer panel. US dealer volumes co-move (Schluter VR = 4.45 vs a cyclic-shift null of 0.44–2.00); foreign IHC volumes do not (VR = 0.73, inside the null). Rank clocks make the GS→JPM equity-revenue swap visible. Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Ad hoc scout: Lovell proportionality finds a sticky JPM–GS swap that gets stronger after the market is removed
articles.dek: A valid, no-tuning alternative to Pearson on compositions (Lovell et al., PLoS Computational Biology 2015). On the PROXY equity-revenue panel, JPM–GS ρ = −0.698 (BH q = 0.021) and −0.882 after residualizing on market factors (q = 0.036); JPM–MS does not survive. Pearson overstates many 14-dealer pairs. Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Secret sauce plans for changeforest, partykit, MARSS and InspectChangepoint
articles.dek: Exactly three avenues per method — Engineering, Math, and a new use on our data — grounded in the 11-10 and 11-11 runs. Top picks are all math: a dependence-aware changeforest test, time-series-valid partykit splits, a short-sample sticky label for the MARSS decomposition (a v0.1-era framework, not a forecast), and an Inspect procedure with the right size under persistent shares. Plans only.

articles.title: changeforest: a random forest that dates regime breaks, once you stop feeding it levels
articles.dek: Rust-core change-point detection that sees volatility and correlation breaks a mean test misses. Reproduced exactly in all three applications; recommended for promotion with a mandatory persistence check, awaiting Jared's approval.

articles.title: Weekly rate and stress regimes: 35 breaks, and a null that finds just as many
articles.dek: On weekly changes of six series the break dates reproduce exactly, but a stationary VAR(1) null produces 20–37 breaks too. Prewhitening leaves 12 stable breaks.

articles.title: Daily volatility and correlation regimes in 9,174 days of rates and VIX
articles.dek: 28 breaks, 23 stable across seeds, zero under both nulls, zero for a mean-change test: this is the use changeforest is built for.

articles.title: Credit spreads have had three regimes since 1990, split in Aug 1998 and Jul 2012
articles.dek: New application: monthly changes of the GZ spread, excess bond premium, VIX and the 10y. Two breaks, both stable, zero under both nulls.

articles.title: partykit trees: readable subgroups that pass on a cross-section and overfit time series
articles.dek: Conditional inference trees and model-based trees reproduced exactly. They clear every gate on 3,074 counties, but a circular-shift null breaks both time-series uses. Recommended (scoped), awaiting approval. A well-known package, so less of a scout find.

articles.title: A VIX-led regime tree for credit spreads: readable, stable, and not real enough
articles.dek: The 4-leaf tree reproduces exactly and VIX wins the root in about 70% of bootstraps. But a shifted response still splits 60% of the time, and the tree loses to the historical mean out of sample.

articles.title: When financial conditions tighten, credit spreads react twice as hard to VIX
articles.dek: A model-based tree splits once, at NFCI 0.057, and beats a calendar break. The catch: shifted state variables split 53% of the time too.

articles.title: Which counties took the biggest unemployment hits in 2008 and 2020
articles.dek: Great Recession damage sorted on pre-crisis unemployment; COVID damage sorted on county size. Both trees clear the null and stay within reach of OLS.

articles.title: Scout: MARSS splits dealer share moves into market, sticky and transient parts
articles.dek: State-space model from ecology (R Journal 2012), run on a PROXY Y-9C dealer-share panel for Q1. GS's equity-revenue-share loss is sticky and mirrors JPM's gain (corr −0.79, BH q = 0.04), while market factors drive 59–74% of quarterly swings for JPM, MS and BAC. Scout recommends it for the promote workflow; not started, awaiting Jared's pick.

articles.title: Scout: InspectChangepoint names which dealers moved at a break, but the breaks fail a persistence null
articles.dek: Sparse-projection change points (JRSS-B 2018), 9.6 ms per panel. On PROXY dealer shares, level breaks (8) are fewer than persistence-matched surrogates produce (12.4–13.3), and drift tests find no significant break: gradual migration, not shocks. Scout verdict: interesting.

articles.method: Interpolated cross-correlation with RSS lag distributions (PyCCF)
articles.title: Scout: astronomers' light-echo timing finds DVP repo follows Form PF reverse repo by six weeks
articles.dek: Interpolated cross-correlation with random-subset-selection lag distributions from reverberation mapping (Peterson et al., PASP 1998; PyCCF V2.2, ported to Python 3 and NumPy at 2e-13 parity, 10x faster), run on public aggregates for Q1: monthly SEC Form PF tab 8.27 against weekly NY Fed fails and OFR repo series, 2013–2025, without regridding. Of five pre-registered pairs only PF reverse repo → DVP volume passes Holm under AR(1) and phase nulls (centroid +39 d, 68% [+31, +54] d, r 0.92, p = 0.001; ZDCF +46 d). On independent series with our persistence the home-field 68% rule finds lags 54–60% of the time, monthly Bartlett bands 75–99%. The lead holds in 2018–21 and flips sign after 2022. Walk-forward miss (−0.24% RMSE vs ARDL, DM p = 0.47). Scout status: interesting; not started.

articles.title: Scout: hydrologists' flood-pooling test picks the right peer groups for short program budgets
articles.dek: L-moment regional frequency analysis from hydrology (Hosking & Wallis 1997; lmomRFA 3.8, Fortran core), run on the SYNTHETIC mock ZBB datasets for Q2: 901 and 1,549 programs with 4–6 years of actual ÷ budget. The heterogeneity statistic H1 calls stated-function regions homogeneous (median −0.09 / −0.05) and rejects discretionary × size (3.56 / 2.34) and random groupings (4.89 / 8.33); it ranks truly mixed regions better than Brown–Forsythe (AUC 0.86 / 0.89 vs 0.81 / 0.85) but has no power edge at matched size. RFA on function regions cuts the q90 error 23–26%, tied with category pooling; discordancy finds planted mislabels weakly (AUC 0.64 / 0.54). Hosking's Cascades example reproduced exactly. Scout status: interesting; not started.
